p4.behavior: 대부분 서술형 계약은 파일 미소비. 실제 CLI help/옵션 검증 인라인을 연결. exit_codes의 10 및 budget_rule/--max-requests·읽기10/수집40/10분120은 S2로 P4 변경.

about: Command-level contracts observed through the real cli.py with a fake Aside (appendix A 38, 45-48, 56, 57, 59-62, 64 and the plan's CLI contract). Each rule is checked by a protocol test in P3; arguments are refused before any request (exit 2) unless stated.

codes.2: arguments, or a handle or file of another query
codes.5: blocked (429, captcha, networkBlocked, unreadable protection state) — a person checks
codes.6: a request or contract failure before any record
codes.8: partial: records then a failure, the command budget, a policy restriction
codes.9: the target cannot be seen (deleted, private, buddy-only, owner-only)
codes.10: the local 10-minute window was full before any record (not an account problem; says when the next request may go)

exit_codes.empty_only_when: 7 is used only for exhausted and window_reached with nothing shown; a capped or stalled empty walk is 8.

sections.fact: A composite command (blog, post, monthly) shows every section, failed ones included, and exits with the most serious failure: 3 and 4 above 5 above 10 above 9 above 6 above 8 above 2 and 7. A failed primary section (the card, the post itself) fails the command.

cases.fact: a non-target failure in a secondary section is partial

schema.fact: schema is generated from the record dataclasses; every field a command can return is described, and no field is described that none returns.

monthly.fact: A month Naver has not published yet comes back as its latest issue: the answer names the issue it actually shows (the mobile API lists issues, so the issue is known rather than inferred).

excerpt.fact: A list's summary is Naver's excerpt, cut at a character count; the text page labels it excerpt (Naver's, cut by length) so its ending is not read as the post's conclusion.

comments_handle.fact: comments asks comments-info once for blogNo (unless the post page already gave it); a continuation handle carries blog_no and the total, so continuing costs no lookup.

post_search_window.fact: post search sends --since/--until as startDate/endDate (Naver applies them) and filters again locally for free; inside-blog search does the same (startDate/endDate measured in the planning session).

post_comments.fact: post --comments reads exactly one page of comments (up to 10 parents shown).

names.fact: --category and topic accept a number (no request) or a name (one request): an exact match first, then a substring; several matches are exit 2 listing numbers; none is exit 9.

feed_empty.fact: An account with no neighbors is an explicit empty result (7) only when Naver says so explicitly (the old feed's hasBuddy false); a missing field is not that. The feed/v1 equivalent is decided in P2.

finished_walk.fact: see paging.json single-page-keeps-its-terminal and capped-keeps-its-terminal: the more: line is offered for an unshown tail, but the stop reason stays the surface's own.

defaults.fact: Default shown records: search, posts, feed, topic 10; comments and buddies 20. --chars 180 for previews (0 = whole); a post body is never clipped.

argument_rules.fact: Combinations a surface cannot honour are refused before they cost a request (P2 R25): posts take --sort, dates and --own-money; blogs only --sort; tags no order (newest first, so dates are applied locally); --blog posts --sort and dates; --blog tags neither.

refused.why: tag search inside a blog ignores order
inside-blog search is posts or tags
popular and notices are one page
the URL already names a category
the directory is one page of names
the flag filters Naver-wide post search only

accepted.why: several words are one query, unquoted
tag search is newest first: a local window closes

budget_rule.fact: Collecting (budget 40) is asking for it: --limit above the command's default, a date window, --out, or images. --limit at or below the default stays at 10 (the old code gave 40 for any --limit).
